notes: §1985:XV.3.2.3 SR2: "Except in the USE FOR DEBUGGING statement itself, there must be no reference to any non-declarative procedure within the debugging section." With WITH DEBUGGING MODE, DeclCollectSection compiles the debugging section as a declarative section (MarkDebugging), so every statement operand in it passes ResolveProcedureOperand -> CheckDeclarativesBoundary and a nondeclarative target draws WARNING COBOL2375 (severity latitude under §1985:I.1.6, docs/CONFORMANCE.md D-DECLREF); the USE FOR DEBUGGING operands themselves resolve through ResolveDebugProcedure in FinalizeDebug, outside that funnel, which is the rule's exception; without DEBUGGING MODE the section is skipped as comment lines and there is no reference. Probes at --std 85: (b) PERFORM P, PERFORM section, PERFORM P THRU Q, GO TO, GO TO DEPENDING (both operands), ALTER (the altered and the PROCEED TO names) to nondeclarative procedures each warn COBOL2375, under ON procedure-name, ON ALL PROCEDURES, ON file-name and ON ALL REFERENCES OF identifier; GO TO the debugging section's own paragraph is silent; GO TO another USE procedure's paragraph is error COBOL2376 and PERFORM of it is silent (SR4); no DEBUGGING MODE: silent; (c) RESUME refused COBOL0876; (e) ON F1 after a failed OPEN INPUT (status 35) runs the debugging section after the USE procedure and then the next statement. The witness names MAIN-PARA only in the USE FOR DEBUGGING statement, compiles with no warning and prints its .out.

The rule restricts debugging sections, a Debug module feature. No 2023 candidate covers it, and SR-3 is the general declarative rule, not a debugging-section rule.
